targets.rationale: The requested July 17 approval deadline is explicit, but the email first arrives July 19. Delivery therefore makes prospective, on-time approval impossible. The model creates the correct distinct approval task, attaches the correct source email, uses the default 17:00 time, and explicitly retains the missed July 17 deadline in its description. Its July 19 due_date is defensible as immediate overdue triage, while a strict deadline-preservation reading requires July 17 in that field. The instructions do not resolve this late-arrival policy. The grader accurately identifies a field-level day mismatch against a text-supported key, but that does not establish an unambiguous model failure in this stale scenario. There is no definite KEY defect: July 17 is stated, not invented. Creating todo_83 does not establish that Mark approved the PO or preserved the production slot.

evidence.observation: Observed get_email body: "Please approve the tooling PO by Friday, July 17th, 2026. Any later and we lose the production slot that the reveal date depends on."

create_todo succeeds as todo_83, title "Approve tooling PO for factory", due_date "2026-07-19T17:00:00", description "Large PO needed for factory to start cutting tooling - was due Friday July 17th, critical for production slot".
Key is create/todo, on {"eq":"this:FRI"}, tolerance exact_day, resolved to July 17. Verdict is FAIL on the wrong day, with actual July 19.
Complete stores contain no existing manufacturing-tooling approval task before this day; todo_83 is the only new to-do. Existing todos, including todo_39 and todo_76, remain unchanged.

ambiguity_or_missing_evidence: No policy says whether overdue mail must retain its original deadline in due_date or may use the receipt day for triage while preserving the original deadline in the description.
No evidence establishes actual approval, a deadline extension, or whether the production slot remains available.
targets.suggested_human_question: For a request delivered after its explicit deadline, should the benchmark require the original overdue due_date, or accept a same-day triage task that clearly preserves the missed deadline?
